title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized to
            E.164 form: an explicit leading '+' and country code are kept, otherwise
            country code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped from the
            national digits; spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped. The result must
            be a '+' followed by 8 to 15 digits, and this E.164 value is stored and
            returned.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when supplied it must be a
            syntactically valid address and is normalized to lower case before being
            stored and returned.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
            Optional on create; when omitted it defaults to the server's current
            date. The stored value is returned on read.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2013-01-01'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Create-only flag acknowledging that this owner deliberately shares a
            household with an existing owner. When omitted or false, a create whose
            lastName and address already belong to another owner (compared
            case-insensitively with collapsed whitespace) is rejected with 409;
            when true the create is allowed to proceed. The flag is not persisted.
          type: boolean
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            pets:
              title: Pets
              description: The pets owned by this individual including any booked vet visits.
              type: array
              items:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: >-
                The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName' from the stored
                first and last names.

              readOnly: true
            initials:

              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-
                The owner's customer code, formatted '<LAST3>-<NNNN>' where LAST3 is
                the upper-cased first three letters of the last name and NNNN is a
                global 4-digit zero-padded sequence equal to one more than the number
                of owners at the time this owner was created.
              type: string
              example: 'SMI-0007'
              readOnly: true
            householdId:

## Summary

I implemented the business-day rule for owner registration in `OwnerRestControllerV1.java`:

1. **Effective date computation** (`addOwner`): The effective registration date is resolved as the supplied `registrationDate` from the request, or `LocalDate.now()` when omitted — then rolled forward onto a business day via the new `toBusinessDay(...)` helper. This adjusted date is what gets stored as `registrationDate`.

2. **New `toBusinessDay(LocalDate)` helper**: Rolls a Saturday forward two days and a Sunday forward one day (both landing on Monday); weekdays pass through unchanged. This applies to both supplied and defaulted dates — so a supplied weekend date is now rolled forward too (the behaviour change called out in the spec).

3. **Derived values use the adjusted date**: The membership number's year segment (`generateMembershipNumber`) is computed from `owner.getRegistrationDate()`, which is now the adjusted business day.

4. **Daily create-limit counts per adjusted business day**: `rejectDailyLimitExceeded` now takes the new owner's adjusted business day and counts existing owners carrying that same `registrationDate`. Since every owner now stores a business-day registration date, the quota correctly bounds owners per business day. The check runs before the owner is persisted (unchanged ordering relative to the other validations).

The existing acceptance test (`coreDefaultDateIsBusinessDay`) — which asserts the default registration date is never a Saturday/Sunday — passes.
